course.title: Circuit Analysis and Electronics
course.title_basis: the header of a course lecture handout
course.instructor_identified_from: not identified: no syllabus survives and the homework prompts carry no instructor name

coverage.notes: All 11 weekly homework prompts survive, and each states the same grading rule, so the problem-set format and what earns credit are known from instructor documents. No completed homework survives anywhere, so nothing shows how a solution was laid out or what the grader accepted. The two test papers and their keys are image-only scans, and the cheat sheets are personal. There is no syllabus. Methods are not covered. The prompts name topics and circuit-simulator tasks but contain no worked solution, and the selected answers at the end of each prompt are final values only. The lab has its own pack (engr204-lab). A lecture writing handout on audience, abstracts, graphing, and conclusions sits in this folder, and it bears on the lab reports, not the homework.

course_policy.summary: No syllabus or generative-AI policy for this course was found. Ask the student to confirm the current policy with the instructor.

precedence: the rules repeated in every one of the 11 prompts
format.prompt_shape: A header with the course, the homework number, the problem count and total points, and the term. Then numbered problems, many with circuit figures, and a Selected Answers list at the end giving final values for most numeric problems.
format.grading_rule: Every prompt says full credit goes to an honest attempt, and that because most answers are given, work must be shown to earn the credit. A bare final answer earns nothing, even when it matches the answer list.

simulator_problems.rule: Circuit-simulator (PSPICE) problems are handed in as printouts or screen captures: the schematic with node voltages or branch currents displayed, or a plot captured from the print preview on a white background.
simulator_problems.plots: Plots need a proper title, axis labels, and a legend. Mark key points with the plotting tool's label feature where the problem asks for values.
simulator_problems.comparison: Several problems ask for written comments on the printout comparing the simulated values with the hand-calculated ones.

what_good_looks_like: Every problem is attempted, and the work shows the method, not just the result, because credit is for the shown attempt.
Where a final answer is listed, the shown work reaches it or explains the discrepancy.
Simulator problems include the requested capture with values displayed or labeled, and a note comparing them to the hand result.
Every plot has a title, axis labels with units, and a legend.
